text:
Samir Rao: Quick pulse from the all-hands 1: which API/Console/Optimize parts are GA vs beta and whatxactly should we say to enterprise customers when they ask for dates?

Priya Nadar: Short version: Core SDK + streaming primitives = GA-target end-Q2; Consoles new per-route dashboards = beta/Q3 early; Optimize suggestion engine = beta/Q3 late. GA for Console/Optimize aimed for Q4 after user feedback.

Elena Ortiz: To be explicit for comms: call out "GA" only when SLA, migration guide, and public docs exist. For anything marked beta, we should offer early access via the Solutions track (Dedicated/Private) but avoid firm dates in public-facing messages.

Marcus Lee: Dev note: the runtime changes for streaming and for prefetching require the new KV layout + a safety fallback. If the 100-token perf matrix shows >5% regression we keep fallback and still ship SDK GA but with lower throughput metrics for that model family.

Tracy Kim: Can we get a plain checklist of what needs to be green for GA vs beta? CS needs to coordinate support staffing.

Priya Nadar: Sure  checklist: 
- GA gates: SLA doc, public migration guide, support runbook, perf telemetries meet SLOs, canary pass with 5 pilot customers.
- Beta gates: internal docs, limited public docs, opt-in pilot list, automated telemetry alerts in Console.

Samir Rao: Nice. Any blockers likely to push the end-Q2 SDK GA?

Marcus Lee: Biggest risk is perf regressions surfaced by the long-tail token workloads. Were running a 72h perf sweep now. If regression >5% across top 10 models we delay some backend optimizations and ship core SDK anyway with a note.

DevOps-bot: deploy-bot: Canary stream-sdk deployment kicked off by @Marcus Lee at 2026-03-23T16:22:01Z  CI: unit tests pass, perf sweep started.

Elena Ortiz: For partners: propose this language - "We expect core SDK streaming to be GA by end of Q2; Console dashboards and Optimize will be available as early access in Q3 with GA targeted for Q4, pending pilot feedback and performance validation."

Tracy Kim: That phrasing works. Ill draft a partner note and ping Priya for final wording.

Priya Nadar: Also: for Dedicated/Private customers, we can offer early toggles for Console dashboards during Phase B. Solutions should coordinate with Marcus for the canary cohort.

Marcus Lee: Plan for canary rollout: 1) internal QA; 2) 3 pilot customers (low-volume); 3) 10 pilot customers (varied workloads); 4) opt-in public beta; 5) GA. Each step ~1-3 weeks depending on telemetry.

Samir Rao: What metrics move us between steps? Define a small set so PM/CS don't over-index.

Priya Nadar: Key metrics: error rate <0.1%, 95th percentile latency within target, no new class of regressions in token-accuracy for reranking/generation; usage behavior (no large abnormal spike).

Tracy Kim: Adding: documentation completeness (migration guide + examples) must be reviewed by Developer Experience before GA announcement.

Elena Ortiz: One more request: if internal pilots show functional issues but perf is fine, we should still treat that as a blocker for GA. Functionality bugs = blocker.

Marcus Lee: Agreed. Ill post perf-sweep results in #eng-runtime by EOD + a short summary for leadership.

DevOps-bot: ci-bot: Perf sweep job #4782 running (step 1/5)  will post summary when complete.

Samir Rao: Perfect. Thanks everyone. Once Marcus posts the numbers I'll approve the partner note wording. :thumbsup:
